deep.reconstruction:
There are no mathematical derivations on this page. It is a sequence of aphoristic notes on method and on Hilbert's self-image as a mathematician, continuing the previous page's reflections on the axiomatic method.

(1) Criticism versus the 'art of systematization'. Hilbert writes that systematizing is often only dull copying work ('stumpfsinnige Abschreibearbeit') that helps no one.

(2) A contrast with Felix Klein. Klein wants mathematics to be the ruler in the world of reality; Hilbert wants to make it ruler of the ideals ('Ideale' is underlined).

(3) A personal motto: not to keep carping but to keep creating is my lot. The interlinear addition 'bin ich da' reads 'that is what I am here for'.

(4) A remark attributed to Poincaré. Reality outdoes the richest poetic fantasy, and nature's colours outdo the most splendid painter's. In the same way, problems arising from physics are richer than problems thought up by the intellect. Hilbert asks why, and then asks what 'anschaulich' (intuitive) means. He proposes a psychological answer: concepts are intuitive when they are more individual and richer in content. That is, they carry more particular relations that interest the memory and therefore stick.
- His example is the memory artist Rückle. Rückle memorizes long digit strings by individualizing each number: he groups the digits in 3s or 4s and relates each group to prime-factor properties or other arithmetic features.
- In the same way we remember novels and events more easily. This holds even though the facts of life and personalities are far more complicated than the most complicated mathematical theories.
- The ** marks a cross-reference whose target is not on this page.

(5) Axiom layers ('Axiomschichten').
- Each deeper layer means a more abstract, more philosophical insight.
- Each higher layer means progress toward the positive side.
- The layers grow like tree rings, and they are the true resting points and stations.
This is the image Hilbert later made public as the 'Tieferlegung der Fundamente' in 'Axiomatisches Denken' (1918).

(6) Programmatic statements.
- 'The axiomatic method is the method of the future.'
- His Grundlagen der Geometrie (1899) should serve as the example. One should enumerate everything that comes up in it ('zur Sprache kommt') and show how it appears newly and clearly ordered.
- 'My life's task is [to unite] the separately transmitted branches of knowledge.' The sentence continues on the previous page, which belongs to the same notebook sequence: '...Zweige zu vereinigen (innerlich durch die Axiomatische Methode, nicht blos äusserlich wie Klein).'

Dating hint (my inference). G. E. Müller published his Göttingen studies of the calculator Gottfried Rückle in 1911–1917, and Hilbert could also have known of Rückle locally. Together with the reference to 'meine Geometrie', this suggests roughly the 1900s–1910s, which fits the axiomatization-of-physics period.
errors: No mathematical content, so no mathematical errors.
Grammatical slip in the original: 'die der prächtigsten Malers' should be 'die des prächtigsten Malers'.
'ich will sie der Ideale machen' is elliptical; the intended sense is 'zur Herrscherin (in der Welt) der Ideale'.

results.what: Programmatic contrast with Klein: mathematics as ruler of the world of ideals rather than of reality
results.modern_name: Hilbert's axiomatic/formal-ideal conception of mathematics versus Klein's applied-intuitive conception
results.usually_credited_to: Hilbert (attitude well documented); the Klein–Hilbert contrast is discussed by Rowe, Corry and others

results.what: Layers of axioms: deeper layers are more abstract and philosophical, higher layers are positive progress, likened to tree rings
Psychological account of 'Anschaulichkeit' as richness of individual memorable relations, illustrated by the calculator Rückle
results.modern_name: Chunking/mnemonic theory of intuitiveness (cf. G. E. Müller's memory research)
results.usually_credited_to: G. E. Müller (Rückle studies, 1911ff.); later chunking theory (Miller 1956)

results.what: Claim that the axiomatic method is the method of the future and that his Geometry is the model case

deep.surprise_reason: These are personal methodological aphorisms consistent with Hilbert's published views ('Axiomatisches Denken' 1918) and with notebook passages already quoted by historians such as Corry and Rowe. The Klein contrast and the Rückle remark are nice biographical colour but are not new results.
transcription_corrections: 'Abschreibearbeit[?]' is plausible, though the hand is unclear; it may be 'Abschreibe-arbeit' with a hyphen.
'Nicht weiter kritteln[?]': the image supports 'kritteln'. The interlinear 'bin ich da.' is placed above 'ist mein'.
'der prächtigsten Malers' as written; the intended reading is 'des prächtigsten Malers'.
'So lernt[?] Rückle' is correct; the name refers to the mental calculator Gottfried Rückle studied by G. E. Müller in Göttingen.
'zähle auf, was dabei Alles nur Sprache Kunst und wie er neu' should most likely read 'zähle auf, was dabei Alles zur Sprache kommt und wie es neu und übersichtlich geordnet erscheint'.
'Meine Geometrie als Beispiel nehmen' is probably followed by a full stop before 'zähle auf'.
